slides.texte_overlay:
Things you should stop doing
as a man in your 20s
Stop saying yes to every plan out of fear of missing out. Three nights out in a row, broke and tired by Thursday. Pick the plans you actually want. The rest will still be there next month.
Stop waiting for motivation to go to the gym. Nobody feels like it at 7am. Put your bag by the door the night before and just go. Discipline is mostly about making it easy for your tired self.
Stop living on delivery apps. Learn three cheap meals you can make in twenty minutes. Your bank account and your body will both notice before the end of the month, and people love a guy who cooks.
Stop comparing your life to highlight reels. Everyone posts the trip, nobody posts the debt that paid for it. Your 20s are supposed to look messy from the inside. That's normal, not failure.

Stop saying "I'm just not a reading person." Five minutes a day of history, art or science is enough to start. You don't need to become a scholar. You just need to stop being proud of knowing nothing.
slides.texte_sophia: I used to say "I'm just not a reading person." Then I started doing five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Turns out I just needed it short.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop ghosting people when it gets awkward. Friends, dates, a job you're leaving. Send the message. "Hey, I don't think this works for me, but thanks." Thirty seconds of discomfort beats a reputation.
Stop sleeping at 3am on work nights. Nothing good happens on your phone after midnight. Protect your sleep like it's part of your job, because the guy who's rested always shows up better.
